props.characteristic: the values report specific individuals that existed independently of this source
props.positive_test: you can name the individual each item is about, and an error in it is an error ABOUT that individual
props.negative_test: fails when no individual is nameable even in principle, only a population or a law (generic); fails when nothing outside the specification is being reported
props.examples: SDSS and LSST imaging of actual objects; fastMRI scans and MIMIC records of actual patients; Wikipedia and Project Gutenberg texts; The Stack's actual repositories; GTSRB's actual street signs
props.notes: D1 `real-particular`, D3 `particular`, and inside D2's `empirical`. The name deliberately says nothing about the KIND of individual -- a galaxy, a patient and a traffic sign are all particulars, and which one it is belongs to `domains`

props.characteristic: no individual is reported, but part of the specification was fixed by measurement or fitting, so "this is unrealistic" is a complaint owed an answer
props.positive_test: a domain expert can argue the source is a poor approximation and the argument has a subject matter; some constant in it traces back to an observation
props.negative_test: fails when nobody claims the source approximates anything real, so "unrealistic" has no purchase (stipulated); fails when specific individuals are reported (particular)
props.examples: CMIP6 climate runs; OC20 and ANI-1x DFT energies; the UVA/Padova type-1 diabetes simulator; PDEBench solver outputs; SERGIO gene-network simulations
props.notes: D1 `real-general`, D3 `generic`; D2 declined this cut and handed it to a queued axis. THIS IS THE CELL THE SPLIT WAS BUILT FOR: the diabetes simulator is `generic` and a locomotion task in the same class of engine is `stipulated`, which is the distinction one value could not hold. D3's open case: PDE benchmarks read `generic` by specification and `stipulated` by falsifiability

props.characteristic: the values answer to an abstract system whose facts EXCEED its specification; a disagreement is settled by computation or proof, never by observation
props.positive_test: the rules are stated in full and yet a value in the data is something that had to be found -- searched for, solved or proved -- rather than chosen
props.negative_test: fails when the specification settles every value directly, so there is nothing to find (stipulated); fails when an observation could settle it (particular, generic)
props.examples: terminal outcomes from the rules of Go and chess; Lean and Coq proof checking; satisfiability of generated k-SAT instances; unit-test pass/fail over real code
props.notes: D2's value, and the one the owner's union restores. D1 derived it as `self-constituting`, then killed it -- "Wikipedia fell to real-particular, authored puzzles to stipulated, nothing left between" -- and D3 met it as its undissolvable recursion trap. That two runs reached the cell and could not keep it, while the third kept it with a working test, is why it is here. FLAGGED: never placed against real names. Its boundary with `stipulated` is the one this axis has not tested

props.characteristic: the generating specification IS the standard; no amount of looking at the world, and no computation, could show an item wrong
props.positive_test: the source cannot be in error, only badly chosen; there is no verification step definable over its items
props.negative_test: fails if some fact about the data had to be discovered rather than declared (formal); fails if anyone is entitled to call it unrealistic (generic)
props.examples: dSprites and Shapes3D factor grids; Erdos-Renyi and stochastic-block-model draws; BBOB analytic test functions; MuJoCo locomotion morphologies; Procgen and MiniGrid levels; Atari frames as rendered
props.notes: Same name and same characteristic in all three runs -- the strongest single agreement on this axis. GRANULARITY IS UNRESOLVED HERE, and all three runs found it: one physics engine spans several values depending on the task modelled (D3), Habitat's scan-then-render case relocates rather than dissolves (D1), and D2 found the value USE-DETERMINED for an engine named as the source -- which contradicts attaching this axis to the entity. See SYNTHESIS.md section 7

props.characteristic: the values answer to something none of the above describes
props.positive_test: a reviewer can say what would show the values wrong and why no value above fits
props.negative_test: not the case where the paper does not say -- that is the `unknown` coding state
props.examples: none named on purpose; D3's unplaceable candidates were normative standards and counterfactual scenarios; D2 considered and declined a `conventional` fourth value
props.notes: the answerable/stipulated split is intended to be exhaustive, so this is expected to stay near-empty. Kept so an ontological miss is recorded as a miss
